app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:189 — set:html directive, current
app/src/pages/index.astro:143 — <script is:inline>, a currently documented directive, not a legacy escape hatch
app/src/pages/index.astro:18 — new URL(Astro.request.url) instead of the canonical Astro.url the docs lead with

latest_apis.rationale: The app sits squarely on the current generation (Astro 7, node adapter 11, server output, current directives) with no deprecated APIs, but it makes no use of Astro 7's newly stable primitives (route caching, Astro.url idiom) and one page hand-rolls what the framework could centralize, so it is current rather than exemplary.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:33 — native fetch + res.json(), no axios-style dependency
app/src/pages/index.astro:145-238 — client script uses URLSearchParams, history.pushState, DOMParser and replaceWith rather than a hydration framework
app/src/pages/index.astro:109-140 — native form controls (type=search input, selects) with real labels; no JS UI library
app/src/styles/global.css:572+ — CSS custom properties throughout and grid layout, per design tokens
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:36-44 — hand-rolled escapeHtml + string-built HTML for the evolution chain, re-implementing the escaping Astro templates give for free
app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:15-31 — hand-rolled concurrency limiter; reasonable, but fetch() here has no AbortController/timeout (pokeapi.js:33)
platform.rationale: It consistently reaches for the platform first (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, DOMParser, pushState, native forms, CSS custom properties) with zero polyfills, but re-implements framework-provided HTML escaping for the evolution tree and omits AbortController on outbound fetches.

evidence: app/package.json:10-13 — exactly two dependencies: astro ^7.4.4 and @astrojs/node ^11.1.9
app/src/lib/pokeapi.js — caching, HTML escaping, sorting and pagination all hand-rolled from platform primitives instead of pulling lodash/query-string/dayjs-style helpers
app/src/styles/global.css:1 — one @import of the required tokens, no CSS framework or icon font (spec-compliant)
dependencies.rationale: Two dependencies, both the current official releases (astro 7.4.x and @astrojs/node 11.1.9 are the latest per the changelog); the node adapter is genuinely required for the standalone npm start contract. Nothing is redundant.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.js — all data access lives behind one module with shared helpers (humanize, enName, cardsFromPokemonRefs), the strongest structural choice here

app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:23-36 — re-implements cardsFromPokemonRefs inline (species dedup, sorting, sprite fallback) instead of reusing/parameterizing app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:129-146; card semantics now live in two places

app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:145-149, moves/[name].astro:40-44, abilities/[name].astro:38-42, types/[name].astro:44-48 — the same try/catch + 404-status + NotFound/Layout wrapper duplicated in every dynamic route; Astro.rewrite('/404') (since astro@4.13.0, current docs) would centralize it

app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:1-46 — plain JS with no JSDoc or TS types for the API payloads; components have interface Props (Layout.astro:3) but the data boundary — the thing the spec says can change at any time — is untyped
app/astro.config.mjs:1-6 — 6-line config, no reliance on internals or experimental flags; an Astro upgrade would touch nothing here
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:30-34, 61-62 — STAT_LABELS/METHOD_ORDER domain constants buried in one page's frontmatter rather than the data layer
churn_resistance.rationale: The single data module, tiny config and zero use of internals mean framework upgrades ripple nowhere, but the copy-pasted card logic, the 404 pattern repeated across four routes and a completely untyped API boundary mean requirement changes (new filters, new card fields, schema drift) ripple through several page files.

findings.issue: Duplicates the card-building logic of cardsFromPokemonRefs (app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:129-146) — species resolution, dedup, ordering, sprite fallback — because it also needs the is_hidden flag.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardsFromPokemonRefs in lib/pokeapi.js to accept an optional per-entry transform (or return the source entry alongside the card) so one implementation owns card semantics.

findings.issue: The not-found pattern (try/catch with err.status !== 404 rethrow, Astro.response.status = 404, NotFound wrapped in Layout) is copy-pasted into all four dynamic routes; every new route must reproduce it or render 404s inconsistently.
findings.suggestion: Centralize with a shared loadResource helper in lib, or use Astro.rewrite('/404') (documented since astro@4.13.0) from each catch so 404 markup and status live in pages/404.astro only.

findings.issue: The data boundary is untyped plain JS — every API field access is dynamic property navigation with no JSDoc or TS types, while the spec explicitly frames the API as a live service whose data can change; schema drift becomes silent runtime breakage.
findings.suggestion: Add TS (Astro supports TypeScript in .ts libs and frontmatter) or JSDoc typedefs for the API payloads consumed by the helpers, so field renames surface as type errors.

findings.issue: fetch() has no AbortController or timeout; a hung upstream request permanently occupies one of the 24 hand-rolled limiter slots and never invalidates its cached promise.
findings.suggestion: Pass an AbortSignal.timeout(...) to fetch and treat aborted/erroring entries as cache misses (the catch on line 43 already covers deletion).

findings.issue: chainToHtml builds HTML strings with a local escapeHtml copy and set:html, re-implementing the escaping Astro templates do automatically; any new field added to chain rendering must remember to escape.
findings.suggestion: Use a small recursive .astro component (Astro supports self-importing components) and let Astro escape values.

findings.issue: Uses new URL(Astro.request.url) to read query params instead of the canonical Astro.url the docs lead with (and which Astro normalizes, with partial pathname decoding documented since v6).
findings.suggestion: Use Astro.url.searchParams / Astro.url directly (same pattern needed at app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:66).

findings.issue: The in-memory promise cache has no TTL or invalidation; fine under the spec today, but any future requirement to reflect data changes within a process lifetime (or bound memory across 1,025 pokemon + moves) means reworking the module's contract.
findings.suggestion: Optional: add a TTL per entry or consider Astro 7's newly stable route caching (Astro.cache.set() with memoryCache()) which standardizes freshness semantics.

findings.issue: Build output (dist/server, dist/client) and the generated .astro/content.d.ts live in the working tree with no app-level .gitignore entry (root .gitignore only covers /data/, /.data-cache/, node_modules/), so generated artifacts are easy to commit accidentally.
findings.suggestion: Add app/.gitignore entries for dist/ and .astro/.

findings.issue: popstate falls back to a full location.reload() rather than reusing the same refresh() partial-render path, causing a full document refetch where the app already has a lighter mechanism.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the existing fetch+DOMParser refresh on popstate, since the URL is already updated by the browser.

summary: This is a lean, current Astro 7 app: two dependencies (both the latest official releases), server output with the current node adapter, and no deprecated APIs — every construct I checked (output:'server', Astro.response.status, set:html, is:inline) is documented as current. The client layer reaches for the platform (fetch, URLSearchParams, DOMParser, pushState) rather than adding tooling. The main age-related risks are inside the app's own code, not the framework choice: duplicated card-building and 404 logic across routes and an untyped API boundary that will ripple when requirements or the data shape move.
